newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-MIAMI OUTLASTS KNICKS TO EVEN SERIES.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-MIAMI OUTLASTS KNICKS TO EVEN SERIES.

text.p: Tim Hardaway's only basket of the fourth quarter, a 15-footer with 49 seconds left, gave Miami the lead for good as the Heat recovered for an 88-84 win over the New York Knicks Friday, tying their Eastern Conference semifinal series at one game apiece.
The best-of-seven series moves to New York for the next two games. Game 3 is Sunday afternoon.

A 10-foot baseline jumper by Allan Houston with 1:13 left gave New York, which trailed by seven at the 5:21 mark, its last lead at 84-83 and capped a 10-2 run. But Hardaway responded with his clutch shot from the foul line, giving him a playoff career-high and franchise-record 34 points.
"I made things happen," said Hardaway.
The Knicks had a chance to take the lead back, but Chris Childs missed a baseline layup after P.J. Brown prevented the New York point guard from passing in to centre Patrick Ewing.
"I knew the last shot was going to be Ewing, but P.J. made a great defensive play and that was the end of that," said Hardaway.
Jamal Mashburn put the game out of reach with a three-pointer from the left wing with 2.9 seconds left as New York opted not to foul to stop the clock.
"I took the shot with confidence. It felt good leaving my hand," said Mashburn about his three-pointer.
Knicks coach Jeff Van Gundy explained his reasons for not fouling down the stretch.

"We didn't want to foul him, we still had timeouts, so we wanted to get a stop," he explained. "We would've been down by one, then we would've played for the last shot with four or five seconds to go."
Alonzo Mourning scored 24 for Miami, which blew a seven-point lead in the final 5:21 but improved to 4-1 at home in the postseason.
Houston had 19 points and Ewing 17 for the Knicks, who lost for the first time in five playoff games this season.

"I feel like we let one slip away," said Ewing, who was limited to 29 minutes due to foul trouble. "We didn't execute well. We let it slip away on the last play. The play was set up for me, but they couldn't get the ball to me.

"We have to do a better job of shutting Tim and Alonzo down. I know I have to get my game back on track. The ball was not falling for me now, but I'm trying to do other things, like rebound and clog up the middle."
Mourning was called for his sixth foul with 1:29 left as he hooked his left arm around Charles Oakley while driving to the lane. Following a timeout, Houston scored to give New York the lead.

"I was disappointed that I wasn't in the game down the stretch," said Mourning. "You just have to play however the referees are calling the game. I just have to grin and bear it. Once they make a call, you can't change it. Patrick got into foul trouble too.
"We have to keep the same kind of intensity Sunday, we can't relax."
Hardaway shot 11-of-24 from the field and 5-of-8 from three-point range.

"His 14 points in a row when we were just not getting anything out of our halfcourt offence showed what he was capable of doing," said Miami coach Pat Riley of Hardaway. "It was a great game for Tim, he made the plays to get us ahead at the end of the game."
John Crotty, normally the backup point guard, had eight points and two assists in 23 minutes.

"It was great to contribute the last two games," said Crotty, who was signed late in the year after playing overseas. "I figured I would get some time tonight and the next thing you know, I'm out there for 23 minutes. Being a ballhandler takes some of the pressure off Tim and it gives him a break to have someone else who can make a play."

"John is a bulldog, he has no fear," said Riley about Crotty. "He can put the ball on the floor, go to the basket and create something. He had a great game tonight. We might not have won the game without John's contributions."
Miami hit 42 percent (28-of-67) from the floor, but committed 21 turnovers that led to 26 points.
All five starters finished in double figures for New York, which made only 38 percent (29-of-77) from the floor and committed only 10 turnovers.
"I think we were overconfident and they played like we were supposed to play," said Houston, who shot 6-of-11 from the field. "They made some shots they didn't make in the first game."
Riley picked up his 1,000th career victory and 141st in the playoffs.
